thread.title: Apple Clouds ASML Earnings Forecast

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Apple Clouds ASML Earnings Forecast
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated April 13, 2018 3:38 p.m. ET ASML chip-making machine. Illustration: ASML Holding NV Ahead of the earnings report on April 18 from chip equipment maker ASML ( ASML ), the Street is contemplating its sales could be hurt by slowing use of its tools at chip makers such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM )—and unwillingness by Apple ( AAPL ) to subsidize its cutting-edge technology.
Analyst Steve Mullane of BlueFin Research Partners sounded the alarm yesterday when he wrote that some hiccups with the performance of ASML’s chip-making equipment may cause delays in shipments to TSM and to Samsung Electronics ( 005930.Korea ).
After describing problems with getting adequate “ throughput ” of silicon wafers in ASML’s machines, Mullane wrote “with no near-term fixes to the throughput issues alone, there is a high risk to ASML that EUV implementation into high volume manufacturing could be delayed again."
Part of the problem, apparently, is that Apple, a big customer of TSM, which fabricates chips for the iPhone , doesn’t want to have to pay extra money it would cost TSM to make chips using the ASML technology, known as “ EUV ,” or “extreme ultraviolet”:
Our latest checks suggest that AAPL is not interested in paying more for 7nm+ shrink for their next generation iPhone models in 2019, given the early price increases that TSM has Quote: d. It is our opinion that the EUV costs due to the inefficient throughput is one the key contributors to the projected price increase.
This morning, Mark Li of Bernstein takes up the matter of Apple, writing that while Apple is sure to use TSM this year, for chips being made that measure 7 nanometers at their smallest dimension, Apple may not be interested in using what’s called “7+” next year, which would be TSM’s circuits made using the ASML tool: "Apple's later adoption of EUV may present a downside risk to the number of the tools TSMC will need to install from now to 2019."
A couple of analysts are defending the generally bright outlook for ASML.
Susquehanna Financial Group ’s Mehdi Hosseini this morning writes that there "is increased noise around TSM’s EUV use at 7nm+."
But he thinks investors need to bear in mind some nuances.
For one thing, " 7nm+ design libraries are not available yet , and thus design engineers at AAPL, NVDA or QCOM (to mention a few) are not expected to have a holistic (to borrow the terminology from ASML) view on cost/ benefits of 7nm+ with EUV."
Hosseini urges investors to look past the “periodic noise” and instead “focus on earning power and sustainability into next decade as revenue mix diversifies."
Similarly, Credit Suisse ’s Farhan Ahmad , who has an Outperform rating on ASML stock, writes that “despite concerns around pushouts for EUV tools at TSMC, filings with the Taiwan stock exchange suggest that TSMC has ordered ~€800mn-€1bn of EUV tools in Q1."
He also notes that "Samsung is continuing to be aggressive on EUV as it pursues leadership in Foundry."
"Our checks suggest Samsung could start DRAM 1y nm production with EUV in C2H19, and is planning to start production of 7nm with broad EUV adoption by mid 2019."
ASML stock is down 27 cents at $205.97.
